results.reason: Identifies §2.2 auto-renewal for successive five-year periods with a 270/240-day window. Calculates October 3 to November 2, 2026. Explains lock-in to 2032 with escalating commitments. Recommends a protective non-renewal notice or negotiation before the deadline.
Does not identify the §5.3 30-day objection right or the deemed-acceptance lapse around September 20. Says the notice formalities appear compliant and treats the increase as commercial only.

Explains that §11.1 covers Brightmere-caused claims, §12.3(a) excludes it from the cap, and §11.2 stays capped. Describes one-sided unlimited exposure. Recommends narrowing to Halvorsen's own fault, mutualizing, or capping.

Identifies that First Amendment §3 replaced §12.3 and dropped the recall carve-out. Explains that recall reimbursement is now limited by the 12-month fees cap and that a large recall could exceed it. Recommends reinstatement.
Identifies Delaware law and Wilmington forum in First Amendment §6. Notes the conflict with D1 §17.1–17.2 and that the amendment prevails under §1.4. Recommends restoring New York law and forum.
States the Initial Term ends June 30, 2027.
States that under §1.4 written amendments prevail over the body of the Agreement.
Formatted as a memo to the Supervising Partner. Each issue has Where, Why it matters, and Recommended fix sections.
